name: How Spring Creates and Wires Beans
overview: Spring knows how to build a bean before the bean exists. Follow what happens between reading the BeanDefinition and calling your first service method.

sections.title: Register the definition
sections.content: Scanning and configuration register BeanDefinitions. They describe how each bean is made, including its scope and construction metadata.

sections.title: Create the instance
sections.content: Spring resolves constructor arguments before it can call the constructor. Other dependencies can be applied afterward through setters or fields.

images.caption: Spring resolves constructor dependencies before it can create the instance.

sections.title: Initialize and expose
sections.content: Initialization callbacks run after dependency injection. A post-processor can wrap the bean in a proxy. The container reuses singletons and invokes managed destruction callbacks on shutdown.

keyPoints: Trace one service from registration to use. Identify when its constructor runs, when its dependencies arrive, and where a proxy can appear.

interviewQA.question: What is a BeanDefinition?
interviewQA.answer: It is the container’s metadata for creating and configuring a bean.

interviewQA.question: Does all injection happen after construction?
interviewQA.answer: No. Constructor dependencies must be resolved first. Setter and field injection occur later.
